end.summary:
Practised predicting and testing whether everyday objects float or sink.
Discussed that material matters, not only weight or size.
Yash identified paper, plastic, dry leaves, and wood as floating; coins, stones, and steel spoons as sinking.
Teach-back was not passed by the end of the lesson.
end.parentNote: Asha practised float-or-sink predictions with everyday objects and asked Yash to explain the role of material, shape, and weight. Yash gave several correct predictions, including that a coin sinks and a log floats; the reasons sometimes focused mainly on heaviness, so this can be revisited. At home, test three safe objects in a bowl of water and record the prediction, result, and material.
